stemBlocks.value: Using a ruler, a pencil and a pair of compasses, construct triangle PQR with PQ = 5 cm, ∠PQR = 60° and ∠QPR = 90°. (ii) Measure and state the length of PR and the measure of ∠PRQ.
Think first: Two angles and the side between them fix the triangle completely, and both angles here — 60° and 90° — are standard compass constructions.

solutionSteps.instruction: Construct a perpendicular to PQ at P.

contentBlocks.value: Equal arcs each side of P on line PQ, then equal larger arcs from those points crossing above P

solutionSteps.instruction: Mark R where the two arms meet and join PR and QR.
Measure PR and find the third angle.

strategyBlocks.value: Draw PQ = 5 cm, construct 60° at Q and 90° at P, and let the two arms meet at R; then measure PR and use the angle sum to check ∠PRQ.

whyThisWorks.value: Angle–side–angle fixes a triangle uniquely, so once the 5 cm side and the two angles at its ends are drawn, the third vertex has only one possible position. The angle sum of 180° then forces ∠PRQ = 30°, and because the triangle is right-angled at P, the tangent ratio predicts PR = PQ tan 60° — an independent check on the drawing.

commonErrors.misconception: Placing the 60° at P and the 90° at Q, which swaps the triangle.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Placing the 60° at P and the 90° at Q, which swaps the triangle.

commonErrors.misconception: Measuring ∠PRQ with a protractor and accepting a badly drawn 29° or 32° instead of checking with the angle sum.

examTip.value: In construction questions, always compute one length or angle by trigonometry first — it tells you immediately whether your drawing is accurate enough for the mark.
